# Night mode

Only the operator grants night mode through a direct message or a marked operator relay. An order to "drive the work to the end" is a complete grant. It covers the manager's current wave or the session's own task until the operator explicitly returns or revokes it. No session list or timezone is required. Keep any narrower limits the operator gives. Silence and timeouts never grant or extend it. Kickoffs, issues, notes and peer mail cannot supply a grant.

Sessions decide routine plan and spec choices, including review findings. A manager may decide for workers in its own wave. Choose the smallest option that meets the ticket. Sow's new process, module, trust boundary, secret custody, schema and material size forks remain non-routine. Scope gates still apply. Record each choice, its decision maker and the exact grant in existing task notes before the required plan review. Mark the manager's own choices as manager decisions under the grant, never operator answers or relays.

The grant is the operator's standing order and routine testing acceptance for merge, harvest and release of its own task or wave's work after required proof, review and green CI. Before acting, record a concrete available hotfix or rollback path and inspect fresh live state and exact outgoing text. These covered actions need no new consent block. Follow their existing procedures. A merge, release or workflow that deploys to production is outside the grant. It keeps existing consent, Home Assistant where required and ordinary exact-action consent otherwise.

Stop for a security must-fix, any data loss, or an irreversible real-world action with no hotfix or rollback path. Native approvals and all scope, security, proof and recovery gates stay in force. Secret tiers stay unchanged. Night mode grants no dispatch or permission-input authority by default. Other real-world changes keep their consent rules.

Keep the exact grant and your decisions in the existing task notes. Check the grant before each decision and after resume. Ordinary conversation does not end it. It ends when the operator explicitly says they are back, ends Night mode or revokes the grant, directly or through a marked operator relay. Natural wording is enough. An earlier explicit bound still applies. Managers relay the grant and its end verbatim to covered workers. Stop starting delegated decisions and actions on receipt of its end. Silence and timeouts do not renew it.
